clue.text: Hock in pot with top tucked in

indicators.note: tucked in says one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: a pot for cooking is a pan

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: put the hock of ham in the pot with the lid on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hock' looks like the ham joint the surface cooks, but it is the verb meaning to pledge at a pawnbroker's.
explanation.definitionFit: To hock something is slang for leaving it with a pawnbroker as security for a loan.

clue.text: After a fight, lion pigs out

indicators.note: out describes the letters being knocked out of their order, as after a brawl

explanation.surface: After a scrap, a lion chases away some pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone 'spoiling for a fight' is eager for one, so the answer stands for 'after (a fight)' in the sense of seeking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoiling for a fight is an idiom meaning eager or itching for trouble, the same as being after it.

clue.text: Sow spared being butchered

indicators.note: butchered means hacked about, so the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A female pig escaped the slaughterhouse after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sow' looks like the female pig of the puzzle's theme, but it is the verb, to scatter seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sow seed is to scatter or distribute it over the ground.

clue.text: Part of custard, say, has extremely greedy people losing face

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word greedy
losing face means the word drops its first letter, its face

parts.note: people are folks

explanation.surface: Greedy people gobble custard and lose their dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. 'losing face' takes the F off FOLKS to leave OLKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper custard is made with the yellow centres of eggs, milk and sugar.

clue.text: Pigs' group said to lack interest

indicators.note: said to signals that the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: a ring of boars, male pigs, would be a boar ring

explanation.surface: Pigs gathered together are reputed to be uninteresting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is an adjective, 'to lack interest' a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull or tedious is said to lack interest, which is what tiresome means.

clue.text: Apart from the top, where the solution goes …

definitions.text: Apart from the top, where the solution goes …

indicators.note: apart from the top means without the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A setter's aside pointing at the grid: this is where your answer belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: lose the W of WHERE, and the result is the place in the grid where you write your solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A solver writes the solution in this very spot, the place being pointed to.

clue.text: With a heave, that's covered pig's head and into the stove it goes

parts.note: a heave of the chest, a sharp intake of breath, is a gasp

indicators.note: covered says the abbreviation wraps round the letter that follows

parts.note: that is, Latin id est, is abbreviated i.e.

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A messy kitchen scene: heaving a covered pig's head into the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'and' are links. IE covers P to give IPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe carrying fuel gas runs into a gas cooker or stove to feed its burners.

clue.text: Part of pig (no residue) gives cold shoulder

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A butcher's note: this cut of pork leaves no waste, and it snubs someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is an idiom for deliberately snubbing or disregarding them.

clue.text: Boatman backs a worker resisting

indicators.note: backs means comes behind, so the setter's letter follows the insect

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself, so the letter is I

explanation.surface: The setter supports a labourer who is holding out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against or opposed to something is being in resistance to it.

clue.text: Without exception, ivy intertwines with tree tops, in my experience

indicators.note: intertwines with says the letters of the two words are twisted together into a new order
tops means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gardener's observation that ivy always winds round trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The tops of 'my experience' are M and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens on each and every occasion happens without exception.

clue.text: What to add to number for when pigs fly till the cows come home

definitions.text: What to add to number for when pigs fly
definitions.meaning: 'when pigs fly' means never; N for number plus EVER placed after it makes that word, so the instruction reads as the answer
an idiom for a very long time, or for good

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is an instruction: put EVER after N (number) and you get NEVER, which is when pigs fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean for an indefinitely long time, endlessly or permanently.

clue.text: Chew pig's tail with crackling

indicators.note: with puts the two pieces side by side
the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: crackling is roasted pork skin, which is the rind

explanation.surface: Gnaw on the pig's tail along with the crunchy roast skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind food is to crush it between the teeth, to chew or masticate.

clue.text: Prepares one to step down where lights are seen

indicators.note: to step down means the letter moves further along the word

parts.note: girds, as in girds one's loins, means prepares for action
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to resign from a job with a view of the lights.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the I steps down two places, GIRDS becoming GRIDS. 'Lights' is crossword jargon for answers entered in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword answers, called lights, are written into the squares of crossword patterns.

clue.text: Praise for Europe set down by one (it's about London)

parts.note: EU is the European Union
to log something is to set it down in writing
one is the Roman numeral I
SE, south-east, is the compass region where London lies

explanation.surface: Applause for Europe written up by someone, explained as being about London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a eulogy is to speak in high praise of someone, often at a funeral.

clue.text: Poke fun at pig

definitions.meaning: to mock or jeer at someone
a verb: to eat greedily, wolf food down

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to jeer at someone and to gobble food greedily.

clue.text: Pig's heart with good bit of chicken

indicators.note: with puts the two pieces side by side
the heart is what is left after the outer letters are taken off

parts.note: a pig is a swine

explanation.surface: A recipe pairing pig offal with some chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig is SWINE, not PIG: its heart is WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken wing is one of the cuts or pieces a bird is jointed into.

clue.text: They'll sell you a porky scratching — it's first on bar back

indicators.note: on says the letter is placed beside the other piece
back says the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a rail is a bar

indicators.note: it's first means the first letter of the word being scratched off

explanation.surface: Pub tale: people selling pork scratchings on the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' is British rhyming slang: porky pie = lie. Pork scratchings are a crunchy British pub snack of fried pig skin.
explanation.definitionFit: People who tell lies, selling you a porky in slang, are liars by definition.

clue.text: Boatman's left no longer stuffing fat pig

indicators.note: stuffing says one piece is packed inside another

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A greedy setter no longer stuffs himself with fatty pork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks the definition as archaic: the old name for the port side of a ship, a boatman's left.
explanation.definitionFit: Before 'port' replaced it, sailors called the left-hand side of a vessel by this old term.

clue.text: Might be in pigs' club

definitions.meaning: pig metal cast from a blast furnace, as in the phrase pig ___
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.surface: Something could happen in a club for pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition points to 'pig iron', crude metal from a blast furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is crude metal from a furnace, and golfers carry numbered metal-headed clubs of this name.

clue.text: Bogus dietitian without a degree is no expert

indicators.note: bogus means fake, so the letters are rearranged into something false
without says some letters are left out of the mix

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for degree, as in the degree symbol of temperature

explanation.surface: A fake nutritionist with no qualification is an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D out of DIETITIAN and rearrange the remaining letters; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer just introduced into a group or skill is a novice rather than an expert.

clue.text: Invite trouble, if a stork flies

indicators.note: flies means the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: If a stork takes off, it is courting danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave in a way that is bound to provoke a bad reaction is an idiomatic way of inviting trouble.

clue.text: Not to be deceived: eating cinders is showing off

indicators.note: eating says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: fly is slang for shrewd, not easily fooled
cinders are ash

explanation.surface: Someone who eats cinders to prove a point is a show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. 'Fly' as an adjective means knowing or sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentatious, gaudy display is a way of showing off, which is what showy flair amounts to.

clue.text: First among characters hailed in each fiefdom

definitions.text: First among characters hailed in each fiefdom

indicators.note: First among means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The leader is the one acclaimed by every vassal in each feudal domain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the head man is first among those hailed in a fiefdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader or head is the person ranked first among all others.

clue.text: Pig's ear made of sacred woods

indicators.note: a pig's ear is British slang for a mess, so the letters are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: A pig's ear turned into something holy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a pig's ear of' is British slang for making a mess of a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees are wood sources, and these conifers are a type of timber tree.

clue.text: Called for peace: change of heart by Katharine Viner

indicators.note: by puts the second piece next to the first
change of heart says the middle letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: peace and quiet is calm
Katharine Viner is editor of the Guardian, the newspaper's own editor, our ed

explanation.surface: The Guardian's editor has a change of mind and demands peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the middle two letters of CALM to give CLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand something loudly and insistently is to call for it noisily, as a crowd does.

clue.text: Part of pig — one, some say, that keeps hot

indicators.note: that keeps says the officer holds the letter inside

parts.note: 'one' refers back to pig; some people call a police officer, a cop, a pig
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A cut of pork that keeps warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pig' does double duty in the surface: a pig is slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork cutlet sliced with the rib is one of the cuts a pig is divided into.

clue.text: Gracious sigh in pig Latin

indicators.note: in pig Latin says the word is put into the children's word game and then spoken

parts.note: in pig Latin the opening consonant goes to the end with -ay added, so sigh becomes ighsay

explanation.surface: A refined exclamation uttered in a joke language.
explanation.walkthrough: Pig Latin moves a word's first consonant to the end and adds -AY; IGHSAY spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gracious! and its mild British equivalent are both exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Palm fern, regularly used after prayer

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the words is picked out

explanation.surface: Palms and ferns are routinely used in religious ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Said at the end of a prayer, the Hebrew word means so be it.

clue.text: Naughty hog intent on getting food!

indicators.note: getting means receiving, so the tent takes the shuffled animal inside it

parts.note: read as in tent: a yurt is a round Central Asian tent

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are disorderly

explanation.surface: A greedy hog is determined to get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intent' looks like an adjective, determined, but splitting it as 'in tent' gives the tent. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultured milk is a common dairy food eaten at breakfast or as dessert.

clue.text: Swine on time for part of pig

indicators.note: on places one piece next to the other

parts.note: a swine is a nasty person, a rotter

explanation.surface: A pig that is punctual, as a cut of pork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' looks like the animal, but it is the insult for a nasty person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot is cooked and eaten as a cheap cut.
